scenario.title: Build the smartest human + AI organization

choiceAvailability.authoredOutcome: Expertise and team resilience grow, at a significant cost in runway and hiring time.
Output rises quickly, while the company becomes more dependent on automated workflows.
Human capability grows without adding headcount; delivery slows during training.
The company learns from customers and starts adoption with a contained pilot.
Work becomes easier to coordinate, though visible product gains take longer.
The organization gains flexibility and trust, while adoption remains gradual.
The company keeps options open and learns more slowly than early adopters.
A cross-functional team can redesign tasks instead of automating them in isolation.
Throughput improves, with more work now relying on the same automated layer.
Capability grows close to the work, at the cost of near-term delivery time.
The service reaches more people and generates a stronger feedback loop.
The company becomes more resilient, while expansion waits for evidence.
Consistency improves, but more teams must coordinate through a small function.
Risk stays contained and the company gives up some near-term scale.
Experts gain broader judgment and teams can improve the whole workflow.
Service capacity grows, while fewer routine cases remain for people to learn from.
Human capability compounds through practice, even as mentoring uses scarce time.
Trust and service resilience increase, though some efficiency remains unrealized.
choiceAvailability.choiceTitle: Keep human review at the customer edge

choiceAvailability.authoredOutcome: Local fit improves, but support and quality become less consistent.
Customers and staff know what to expect, with slower initial rollout.
People retain a path into new roles, reducing short-term cash for expansion.
Trust grows and customers can make informed choices about the service.
The company gains a new market path, but delivery requires more review.
Access grows beyond the company, with less control over how the tools are used.
Collective knowledge improves, while some market advantage is shared.
Productivity and adoption rise, with more critical operations linked to automated decisions.
Capability and resilience improve across the network, at a cost in time and capital.
Reliability deepens while the company passes on some immediate market reach.
Dependence falls and resilience rises, using resources that could fund expansion.
Output and adoption rise, along with the cost of interruption or oversight failure.
Knowledge accumulates across teams instead of staying with a few specialists.
The company gains a growth option while taking on more dependence.
Shared documentation improves capability and resilience, even without a large specialist bench.
choiceAvailability.choiceTitle: Document how the work gets done

choiceAvailability.authoredOutcome: Resilience improves, although duplicate capacity is less efficient in the short term.
Growth accelerates, but teams have less room to absorb surprises.
